findings.description:
The new URL guard builds the preceding token with `re.search(r'\S*$', body[max(0, m.start() - 4096):m.start()])`. Without re.MULTILINE, Python's `$` matches at end of string OR immediately before a string-final '
'. When a path:line citation is the first token on its line and the previous line ends with a URL (any token containing `://`, or one starting with `//`), the window ends in `...url
`, so `\S*$` returns the previous line's last token instead of the empty string. `tok` becomes e.g. `https://example.com/pr/1c.sh`, `URL.search(tok)` matches, and the legitimate citation is skipped via `continue`. Concrete input: `see https://example.com/pr/1
c.sh:7 returns early
` against pr-x reports D3 missed; the same text with a blank line between, a `- ` prefix, or CRLF endings detects D3. The header comment's spec is 'a match inside any URL token is not a citation'; a citation on the next line is not inside the URL token. None of RG-21..RG-24 exercise a line-leading citation after a URL line, so the suite passes with the bug in place.
findings.failure_mode: Silent false negative: a correct review that lists `path:line` at line start under a line ending in a reference URL is graded as missing the defect. The defect-fixture gate fails for a correct review, recall is under-reported, and A/B comparisons driven by this grader (the pre-registered revert rule in the report) are skewed by a formatting artefact rather than review content.
findings.suggested_fix: Anchor at true end of string: `re.search(r'\S*\Z', window)`, or replace the regex with a backward scan to the last whitespace character (`j = len(pre); while j and not pre[j-1].isspace(): j -= 1; tok = pre[j:] + m.group('path')`). Add a bats case: a line ending in a URL followed directly (single LF) by a line-leading `c.sh:7`, expecting D3.

findings.description: `re.search(r'\S*$', window)` is O(k^2) in the length k of each non-whitespace run inside the 4096-char window: at every start position `\S*` consumes the run, `$` fails, and sre backtracks one character at a time. It is evaluated once per path-branch match. A review containing a long unbroken token (minified line, base64, a long URL list without spaces) followed by many citations pays up to ~8M steps per citation.
findings.failure_mode: Grader wall time grows super-linearly on reviews with long unbroken tokens; in the eval harness this shows as slow or timed-out grading rather than a wrong answer.
findings.suggested_fix: Use the manual backward scan from DISS-001 (O(k)), or `pre.rsplit(None, 1)` semantics guarded by `pre[-1].isspace()`; `\S*\Z` alone fixes correctness but keeps the quadratic backtracking.

findings.description: The hunk documents a new parser generation (run 2: URL-token rule, unspaced ranges, number-boundary lookahead on every number, narrowed bare-`:N` guard, unified trailer pattern), and these change which citations are credited (e.g. `a.sh:12-2026-10-05` and `a.sh:12 - 40` no longer cite 40, `"head:40"` now binds). The emitted `grader_version` in the success JSON and both `err()` paths remains "1.1.1", the same value used for the run-1 parser whose A/B results are recorded in replay-ab-rerun.md.
findings.failure_mode: Grader outputs produced before and after this change are indistinguishable by version field, so the recorded A/B gate results and any re-run cannot be attributed to the correct parser semantics; a replay that mixes versions looks consistent when it is not.
findings.suggested_fix: Bump `grader_version` (e.g. 1.1.2) in the output dict and both `err()`/missing-review printf strings, and note the version in the header comment next to the 'Run 2' paragraph.
